# Standards Board {#sec-art-IHXJUPV0}

## Preface {#sec-art-22W5QO3O}

1. This section’s purpose is to provide additional details to the Chapter Standards Board Hearing Procedures described in the International Bylaws ({{< var acronyms.ibl >}}), as well as to describe the procedure for Academic Review. For more detailed procedures on Chapter Standards Board Trials, refer to {{< var acronyms.ibl >}} Article V, Section 22.1

## Purpose {#sec-art-W45W9VZK}

1. To determine responsibility for possible infractions of these Local Bylaws, Chapter legislation, and standards of the chapter, as well as all other laws and rules brothers must adhere to as defined in {{< var acronyms.ibl >}} Article V, Section 22(a).
1. To be prepared to take immediate action following an accusation calling for suspension or expulsion, as in {{< var acronyms.ibl >}} Article VI, Section 13(b)(4)
1. To determine sanctions on brothers found to be responsible for previously defined infractions, as detailed in {{< var acronyms.ibl >}} Article V, Section (j)(10)
1. To assist the President and the Vice President of Health and Safety in establishing chapter safety standards.
1. To facilitate appropriate remediation for those who fall short of their obligations to Theta Chi Fraternity.
1. To incentivize brothers to achieve chapter standards.

## Operations {#sec-art-PO1G09NO}

1. Composition, term of office, membership of at-large members, vacancies, the chairman, and the voting procedures shall be determined by {{< var acronyms.ibl >}} Article V, Sections (a-i).

1. The Quorum of the Chapter Standards Board will be the entirety of its members.
   a. The board can meet for purposes other than a Chapter Standards Board Hearing without the entirety of its members.

1. The votes of the board are by {{< var glossary.simple-majority >}}

1. If, at any time, an at-large member becomes ineligible to hold office or is elected to an Executive Council ({{< var acronyms.ec >}}) position, that at-large member is immediately removed from the board.

1. Otherwise, at-large members can only be removed by an Absolute Supermajority vote of the active chapter as detailed in {{< var acronyms.ibl >}} Article V, Section 22 (e). An at-large member of the board should be brought up to the chapter by the Vice President for removal from the board for the following reasons:
   a. Failure to perform their duties, including unexcused absence from more than one board meeting per semester.
   a. Failure to maintain the confidentiality of all board proceedings.
   a. Conduct unbecoming of an at-large member, or that negatively affects the credibility of the board.

1. Details of every ongoing trial, or trials that end with a non-responsible verdict, are private.
   a. Board members inappropriately discussing trials outside the Chapter Standards Board meetings will be brought to the Chapter Standards Board by the Vice President or Chaplain.
   a. The details of trials that end with a responsible verdict will be kept by the Vice President and the Chaplain in a secure location and will only be accessed by the Vice President or the Chaplain when they are needed for a Chapter Standards Board trial.

## Hearing Procedure {#sec-art-1D0EJQ7H}

1. All accusations must be submitted in writing to the Vice President within three months of the most recent violation, excluding the winter and summer breaks defined by the University.

1. Upon receiving the Accusation, the Vice President will decide within forty-eight hours of the accusation whether or not a hearing will take place ({{< var acronyms.ibl >}} Article V, Section 22(j)(2)).

1. If there is to be a hearing, the Vice President will then decide whether the hearing will be a Chapter Standards Board Hearing.

1. If the Vice President decides there will be a hearing, the Vice President will provide written notification to the accused.
   a. The notification must be given within ninety-six hours of receipt of the accusation (including the forty-eight hours to decide whether or not a hearing will take place).
   a. The notification must include the accusations as submitted to the Vice President, with enough detail to allow the accused to prepare a defense.

1. Upon receiving the notification, the accused has twenty-four hours to submit a plea in writing to the Vice President.
   a. The possible pleas are {{< var glossary.responsible-plea >}}, {{< var glossary.not-responsible-plea >}}, and {{< var glossary.no-contest-plea >}}.
   a. If a plea is not received within the twenty-four hours specified above, a {{< var glossary.no-contest-plea >}} will be entered.

1. After a plea is entered, the Vice President will have a week to schedule a time and place for the hearing.
   a. The hearing shall occur between 1 and 3 weeks after a plea is entered.
   a. The Vice President will notify the accused, accuser, the Chaplain, and the at-large members of the time, date, and location of the hearing within twenty-four hours of scheduling the time and place.

1. The Vice President will inform the {{< var acronyms.ec >}} of the accusation, the accused, and the nature of the complaint at the next {{< var acronyms.ec >}} meeting.

1. Members of the board will recuse themselves from the hearing if they feel a conflict of interest exists or if they are the accused.
   Members of the Chapter Standards Board may be recused by a Simple Majority vote of the remaining members. a. The accused, accuser, or a member of the board may call for such a vote.
   a. The recusal process must be completed before the trial starts, during the 1 to 3 week period before the trial.
   a. Vacancies due to recusal should be filled in accordance with {{< var acronyms.ibl >}} Article V, Section 22(j)(9)(v) or (vi), as they apply to the situation.

## Hearing Preparations {#sec-art-HEKXL782}

1. Evidence and a statement by the anonymous accuser will be distributed by the Vice President to all members of the Chapter Standards Board between twenty-four and forty-eight hours before the hearing date and time.
1. Witnesses may be called by the accuser or the accused for the trial. Any such witnesses must state their intent to participate and their stance at least three hours before the trial to the Vice President.
   a. The witnesses may instead volunteer by giving the Vice President a written statement.
1. Witnesses will not discuss the hearing or the accusation outside of the hearing.
1. The dress at the hearing will be informal.
1. The Vice President will call the hearing to order and ask all but the members of the Chapter Standards Board and the Chapter Advisor (if he is present) to leave the room.
1. The Chapter Standards Board may request current or former First or Second Guards to watch over the witnesses outside the room during the hearing.

## Hearing Method {#sec-art-L96ICVPJ}

1. The accused will be invited into the room.

1. The Vice President will read aloud the charges and ensure that the accused understands the charges.

1. The accused may give a statement with a reasonable time limit as voted on by the Chapter Standards Board.

1. The accused may then be asked questions by the members of the Chapter Standards Board and the {{< var glossary.chapter-advisor >}} (if he is present), with a reasonable time limit as voted on by the voting members of the Chapter Standards Board.

1. The accused shall leave the room, and the witnesses will be brought in one by one by the Vice President.

1. Witnesses who wish to speak for the charges will be chosen in an order decided by the Vice President to give a statement with a time limit as voted on by the Chapter Standards Board.

1. The {{< var glossary.chapter-advisor >}} (if he is present) and members of the Chapter Standards Board may ask questions of the witness(es) with a time limit as voted on by the Chapter Standards Board.

1. Witnesses who wish to speak against the charges will be chosen in an order decided by the Vice President to give a statement with a time limit as voted on by the Chapter Standards Board.

1. The {{< var glossary.chapter-advisor >}} (if he is present) and members of the Chapter Standards Board will ask questions of the witness(es) with a time limit as voted on by the voting members of the Chapter Standards Board.

1. All witnesses will be excused by the Vice President.

1. The Chapter Standards Board will determine if the accused is {{< var glossary.responsible >}} or {{< var glossary.not-responsible >}} for the accusations brought forth against him.
   a. Any member of the Chapter Standards Board may recall any witnesses or the accused, if further questions arise. This may be done once per witness. To recall a witness more than once requires a unanimous vote of the voting members of the Chapter Standards Board.

1. The Chapter Standards Board will then determine appropriate sanctions, if any.
   a. Past judicial history of the accused and sanctions given for similar accusations in the past may be considered.

1. After the sanctions have been determined, the Vice President will readmit the accused back to the hearing and will announce the sanctions given, if any.

1. The Vice President will then inform the accused of the appeal process.

1. The Vice President will then adjourn the hearing.

## Sanctions {#sec-art-S2YKROAM}

1. The board may issue sanctions within its scope as defined by {{< var acronyms.ibl >}} Article V, Section 22(j)(10). The board may put time limits on the completion of the sanctions. The following is an incomplete set of examples of possible sanctions:
   a. Community Service
   a. Cost of repairs
   a. Fines
   a. House Service and/or extra details
   a. Letter of Apology
   a. {{< var glossary.staggard >}} status
   a. {{< var glossary.grade-improvement-plan >}}
   a. {{< var glossary.bad-academic-standing >}}
   a. Removal from an Appointed Position
   a. Request for completion of a training course
   a. Recommendation for suspension
   a. Interim Suspension

1. The Vice President will ensure the completion of sanctions.
   a. If the sanctions are not completed, the Vice President will bring the brother up for standards, with the possibility of recommendation for suspension.

## Appeals {#sec-art-EM09V7RF}

1. A decision of the Chapter Standards Board may be appealed once, as detailed in the {{< var acronyms.ibl >}} Article V, Section 22(j)(11).
   a. Appeals must be submitted within 7 days after receiving written notification of the results of the hearing.
   a. If an appeal is made, the confidentiality of the hearing is waived starting at the next regularly scheduled chapter meeting at which a quorum is present.
   a. The appeal will be scheduled as the first New Business of the Chapter meeting.

1. The appeal will be presented in writing to the Vice President and will state the grounds for the appeal.

1. At the next chapter meeting during the appeal motion, the appellant will start by explaining the reason for the appeal. The Vice President will then explain the board’s decision and its reasons. Following the statements, a discussion will take place. The chapter may overturn the sanctions with a ¾ vote in favor of all chapter members present and eligible to vote.

1. If the decision is overturned, the chapter may give new sanctions by a {{< var glossary.simple-majority >}} vote.

1. Each decision of the Chapter Standards Board can be appealed only once.

## Academic Review {#sec-art-HL5IIDEQ}

1. An Academic Review shall be held whenever the Scholarship Chair requests an Academic Review in accordance with the duties of their office.

1. An Academic Review is not a Standards Board Hearing.

1. An Academic Review shall be carried out by the Scholarship Chair and the members of Standards Board.

1. A {{< var glossary.quorum >}} of Standards Board is required to hold an Academic Review.

1. Attendance of an Academic Review is mandatory for all members of Standards Board and the Scholarship Chair.

1. A member of Standards Board may be recused from an Academic Review under the following circumstances:
   a. Members of the board for whom the Scholarship Chair is requesting a suspension trial will recuse themselves.
   a. Members of Standards Board will recuse themselves if they feel a conflict of interest exists.
   a. Members of Standards Board may be recused by a {{< var glossary.simple-majority >}} vote of the remaining members of Standards Board. The brother under review, the Scholarship Chair, or a member of Standards Board may call for such a vote.

1. Process of an Academic Review

   a. Scheduling:
      i. The Vice President will schedule Academic Reviews.
      i. All Academic Reviews for a semester shall be held at the beginning of the semester at the discretion of the Vice President.
      i. Members of Standards Board of whom the Scholarship Chair has requested an Academic Review will have their Academic Reviews completed before the Academic Reviews of brothers not on Standards Board. If the Scholarship Chair has requested an Academic Review for the Vice President, the Academic Review for the Vice President will happen first.
      i. The Vice President will inform the board, Scholarship Chair, and brothers under review of the day's schedule within three days of the Scholarship Chair requesting academic suspensions.

   b. Preparation:
      i. The brother under review is not required to {{< var glossary.attend >}}.
      i. Both the brother under review and the Scholarship Chair may provide witnesses and any form of relevant documents, including written statements. If either the brother under review or the Scholarship Chair cannot {{< var glossary.attend >}} the review, any such documents must be sent to the Vice President along with an order of any witnesses to be called.
      i. The Vice President will call the meeting to order and ask all but unrecused members of the board, the Scholarship Chair, and the brother under review to leave the room.

   c. Method:
      i. The Scholarship Chair and brother under review may give an opening statement, in that order.
      i. The Scholarship Chair may then be asked questions by the brother under review and the board.
      i. The brother under review may then be asked questions by the Scholarship Chair and the board.
      i. The Scholarship Chair and then the brother under review may then present any witnesses or documents. If they are not present, the provided witnesses and documents will be presented in the provided order. After each witness gives a statement, the Scholarship Chair, brother under review, and members of Standards Board may ask questions of the witness. Documents will remain with the Vice President until the conclusion of the review.
      i. The Scholarship Chair and brother under review may give closing statements in that order.
      i. The Vice President will excuse the Scholarship Chair and brother under review.
      i. The members of Standards Board will then deliberate. The members of Standards Board may consult any documents and recall any witnesses, the Scholarship Chair, or the brother under review if further questions arise.
      i. The voting members of Standards Board will vote to either recommend the brother under review for suspension, or to not recommend the brother under review for suspension.
      i. The Vice President will recall the Scholarship Chair and the brother under review and inform them of the decision made by Standards Board.
      i. If Standards Board voted to recommend the brother under review for suspension, the Vice President will immediately inform the President of the decision made by Standards Board and request a suspension trial for the brother under review.

1. In the event that Standards Board does not recommend the brother under review for suspension, the proceedings of the review will remain confidential.

1. In the event that the board recommends the brother under review for suspension the proceedings of the review will not be confidential. Any statements by the Scholarship Chair, brother under review, or witnesses, the content of any presented documents, and the nature of the deliberation done by Standards Board may be requested and discussed during the associated suspension trial.
